articles.title: Billionaire Bill Ackman Says There’s a Huge Disconnect in Wall Street’s Expectations for Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Alphabet
articles.summary: Bill Ackman argues that Wall Street analysts are underestimating the revenue growth potential from the massive capital expenditures being made by Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Alphabet in AI data centers. He estimates these companies can generate 15-25% returns on invested capital from their data center buildouts, suggesting consensus estimates for minimal revenue growth are too pessimistic. At current valuations of 21-28x forward earnings, all four companies appear undervalued, with Alphabet and Meta being particularly attractive.

articles.title: Why Advanced Micro Devices Stock Surged This Week
articles.summary: AMD stock rallied 19% this week driven by strong AI infrastructure spending signals and a major deal with Google Cloud to supply 5th Gen EPYC server processors. CoreWeave's raised capital expenditure guidance to $37-39 billion and Google Cloud's selection of AMD processors for confidential computing systems reinforced investor confidence in sustained data center demand. However, AMD's elevated P/E ratio of 117.6 leaves little room for error, with future performance dependent on maintaining hyperscaler capital spending momentum.

articles.title: The Blockchain Boom Is Still Happening Behind the Scenes. These 3 Growth Stocks Will Benefit.
articles.summary: Blockchain technology is being integrated silently into mainstream products and services rather than being promoted as a standalone technology. Three growth stocks are well-positioned to benefit from blockchain expansion: Block (formerly Square) is pioneering blockchain-enabled fintech services, IBM's enterprise blockchain platform is solving real-world problems in supply chain and food safety, and Amazon Web Services powers most public blockchains and is experiencing accelerating cloud growth.

articles.title: What's Going on With CoreWeave Stock?
articles.summary: CoreWeave delivered quarterly financial results that impressed the stock market and investors. However, the stock fell over 6% on November 13, 2026, amid AI-cloud selling pressures and reported $4 billion loan talks. Despite challenges from competitors like Microsoft, Oracle, and Nebius Group, CoreWeave reports AI demand is 10 times its capacity through 2027.

articles.title: Qualcomm Is Cheap Enough to Hold Through 2030
articles.summary: Qualcomm stock has fallen 33% from its May high and now trades at just 9.6x management's fiscal 2029 earnings target, making it attractive for long-term investors. While handset chip sales have declined 26% year-over-year, the company is building a new growth engine through its data center business, which is forecast to reach a $7 billion annual run rate by end of fiscal 2027. With Amazon as a key customer and a $60 billion purchase option contract, Qualcomm's diversification into data center, automotive, and IoT segments is expected to grow over 60% in fiscal 2027, offsetting losses from Apple's shift to proprietary modems.

articles.title: Sundar Pichai Reported Alphabet's Cloud Revenue Grew 103% Last Quarter While the Gemini App Reached 1 Billion Monthly Users. Is Google Cloud Becoming a Bigger Growth Driver Than Search?
articles.summary: Alphabet reported Google Cloud revenue grew 103% year-over-year to $30.7 billion in Q3, while the Gemini App reached 1 billion monthly users. However, Google Search growth slowed to 12% from 17% in Q2, raising concerns about AI's impact on search monetization. Cloud is emerging as Alphabet's primary growth engine with a $561 billion customer backlog, but the stock fell 28% from its peak amid worries about search's long-term viability and massive capital spending pressures.

articles.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 13: Cerebras Surges Over 11% on Record Q3 Revenue and Raised 2026 Guidance
articles.summary: Cerebras Systems surged 11.22% after reporting record Q3 revenue of $210.8 million (55% YoY growth) and raising 2026 guidance. The company added Microsoft as a customer alongside Oracle and Amazon. The stock rally was also supported by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, potentially opening market share opportunities for Cerebras.

articles.title: Gatekeeper Now Available to Buy in AWS Marketplace, Giving Compliance-Driven Organisations a Faster Route to Vendor Governance
articles.summary: Gatekeeper, a unified Vendor and Contract Lifecycle Management solution, is now available for purchase through AWS Marketplace. The platform consolidates vendor risk, contracts, compliance and spend management into a single system, with AI agents running exclusively on Amazon Bedrock to keep customer data in-region. This enables compliance-driven organizations to streamline vendor governance through their existing AWS accounts.

articles.title: Kaplan Fox Alerts Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL, GOOG) Investors to a Securities Class Action Lawsuit – Contact the Firm Before Deadline on December 1, 2026 for Leadership Role
articles.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a securities class action lawsuit against Alphabet Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased shares between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Alphabet made false statements regarding its Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model, concealing disappointing training results and significant launch delays. Following Bloomberg's report of the delays on July 16, 2026, Alphabet's stock price fell 4.4%. The deadline to move for lead plaintiff status is December 1, 2026.

articles.title: CBRS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on Strong Cloud Growth
articles.summary: Cerebras Systems (CBRS) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 13 cents per share, beating estimates, with revenues surging 70% year-over-year to $230.87 million. Cloud revenues soared 272% to $144.91 million driven by AI inference demand and higher pricing. The company secured partnerships with Oracle and Microsoft, raised 2026 revenue guidance to $940-$960 million, and expects to triple revenues in 2027 with expanding data center capacity.

articles.summary: Alphabet has been attracting investor attention despite a -14.5% decline over the past month, significantly underperforming the S&P 500's -2.6% drop. While the company shows strong revenue growth projections of 26.7-32.2% for the current and next fiscal years, earnings estimate revisions have declined by 3.4% over the last 30 days. The stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term, and is trading at a discount to peers with a B valuation grade.

articles.title: Investors Heavily Search Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN): Here is What You Need to Know
articles.summary: Amazon stock has gained 5% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500's -2.6% decline. While current quarter earnings are expected to grow 26.7% year-over-year, the consensus estimate has declined 3.3% in the last 30 days. Amazon holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with a D valuation grade, indicating it trades at a premium to peers and is expected to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

articles.title: Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
articles.summary: Alphabet (GOOG) has been trending on Zacks.com with shares down 14.4% over the past month, significantly underperforming the S&P 500's -2.6% decline. While the company shows strong revenue growth projections of 26.7-32.5% for the current and next fiscal years, recent earnings estimate revisions have been negative (-4.1% over 30 days for current quarter). The stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

articles.title: What's Wrong With Amazon.com (AMZN) Stock, and Is It a Buy in November?
articles.summary: Amazon stock has gained 9% over the past year, below its historical averages, but the company remains fundamentally strong with 12% revenue growth, record operating margins of 13.9%, and AWS cloud revenue surging 39% year-over-year. While concerns exist around slowing e-commerce growth, heavy AI capital expenditures, and shrinking free cash flow, the author recommends Amazon as a buy for long-term investors given its reasonable forward P/E ratio of 25 (below its five-year average of 38) and strong growth metrics.

articles.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has Nearly $110 Billion Invested in These 2 Tech Stocks
articles.summary: Under new CEO Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway maintains significant positions in Apple ($79.4B) and Alphabet ($30.4B), together comprising over 30% of its stock portfolio. While Apple's stock has surged 28% this year due to disciplined AI spending and strong iPhone sales, Alphabet's stock has declined 8% amid concerns over massive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure. Despite near-term headwinds, both companies are considered long-term buys given their competitive advantages and valuations.

articles.title: Qualcomm's $5 Billion Data Center Ramp Puts Execution in Focus Now
articles.summary: Qualcomm is transitioning its data center business from development to commercial revenue, targeting $5 billion in fiscal 2027 sales with over $650 million expected in Q1. The company has secured a major deal with Amazon covering up to $60 billion in potential purchases over 10 years. However, early concentration with two hyperscaler customers, margin pressure, and declining fiscal 2027 EPS projections present execution risks as Qualcomm competes against established rivals like NVIDIA and AMD.

articles.title: Few S&P 500 Stocks Yield Over 5%. Here's My Top Pick to Buy Now.
articles.summary: With Treasury yields rising above 5%, dividend stocks are becoming less attractive. However, UPS stands out as one of only ~20 S&P 500 stocks offering yields over 5% at 5.8%. After stabilizing its business by pivoting away from low-margin Amazon deliveries and securing higher-margin customers, UPS is expected to grow revenue 4% and adjusted EPS 2% in 2026. Trading at 15x adjusted EPS with 16 consecutive years of dividend increases, UPS offers a reliable income play for conservative investors.

articles.title: Best Health & Fitness Stocks to Buy on Strong Market Potential
articles.summary: The global health and wellness market is projected to reach $7.76 trillion by 2035 with a 4.94% CAGR, driven by increased consumer spending on fitness, preventive care, and digital health tools. Major technology companies like Apple and Amazon are expanding health-related offerings, while specialized companies in fitness apparel, wearables, and sports equipment are capitalizing on shifting consumer preferences toward personalized wellness solutions.

articles.title: SpaceX's Expanding Ambitions: ETFs to Play Its Next Growth Phase
articles.summary: SpaceX is diversifying beyond rocket launches into AI infrastructure, satellite communications, and lunar operations. The company secured a spot in NASA's $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services program and signed major cloud services deals with Anthropic ($1.25B/month) and Google ($920M/month). Q3 2026 results showed 161% revenue growth to $14.6B with $4.4B net income. Three space-focused ETFs offer significant SpaceX exposure.

articles.title: atQor Named Finalist for 2026 Microsoft Partner of the Year Award in - Agents
